details:
I’d like to share some thoughts regarding the recent UI changes, especially the new Shop button.

While I understand the need for sustainable monetization, the current placement and prominence of the Shop button may unintentionally disrupt the user experience that made VRChat unique.

Here are a few suggestions for improvement:

Respect existing user habits.

Restore the original core buttons (Home, Respawn, etc.) to their familiar positions. Long-time users rely on muscle memory, and sudden changes can create unnecessary frustration.

Make the Shop visible but not dominant.

Keep it accessible — for example, in the upper corner or under a “More” menu — but don’t let it interrupt the user’s established flow.

Integrate the Shop naturally into the experience.

Instead of forcing visibility through the main UI, let users discover the Shop through interactions:

Clicking a friend’s avatar → “View in Shop”

Visiting creator worlds → “Support this creator”

Exploring featured community events tied to Shop content

Connect the Shop with Live Instances.

The new Live Instances feature has great potential for community engagement.

Allowing creators to attach or promote their Shop listings within these active event instances (for example, through in-world support buttons or banners) would encourage organic support and highlight VRChat’s social spirit — without breaking immersion.

Focus on community, not commerce.

The strength of VRChat has always been freedom and creativity. The Shop should feel like a celebration of creators, not just a storefront.

By making the Shop a natural part of VRChat’s culture — rather than a marketing element — you can maintain its core identity while still supporting a healthy business model.

Thank you for your continuous effort and passion for improving the platform.
title: Feedback on the New UI and Shop Button Placement
